steps.text: Combine water, onion, tomato, lentils, oil, cumin, and salt in a large pot over medium heat; bring to a boil. Boil, stirring occasionally, until lentils are soft, about 30 minutes.
Add potatoes; cook until tender, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Colombian Lentils
raw_recipe.description: This Colombian lentil recipe is made with tomato, onion, and potatoes. It’s great to serve as a first course or with hot, fluffy rice for a main dish.
raw_recipe.name: Colombian Lentils

recipeInstructions.text: Combine water, onion, tomato, lentils, oil, cumin, and salt in a large pot over medium heat; bring to a boil. Boil, stirring occasionally, until lentils are soft, about 30 minutes.
Add potatoes; cook until tender, about 15 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I had to add more liquid as it cooked and I added chicken broth instead of water. My Colombian boyfriend said it was like his mother's. :)

This was perfect for our flu. I added/modified to the recipe using 1 cup of lentils. I sauteed onions and cumin seeds, then added garlic, tomatoes, then carrots. Added a carton of stock and lentils. Simmered. Added potato. Simmered. Then seasoned to taste. Salt. Pepper. Dash of turmeric. Half a lemon. Served with warm, rustic bread. Delish.

Fantastic and healthy recipe that you will become addicted too. 
I used whole green lentils, which have a great earthy flavour but will stay hard if you add the salt at the beginning of cooking, I added the salt when I put the potatoes in.
I also added 4 extra Half cups of boiling water during the cooking. I read another review before trying this and they said they wish they had had made double, "I agree", this recipe is for 3 small starter sized portions which actually served me and my Son as a main with some crusty bread. I would have added a photograph but it has all gone, still, it won't be long before I make a double portion of this again.
One little tip; Grind whole cumin for the best flavour, I always do and it makes a massive difference.

I'm new to cooking lentils, and this looked intriguing. Noting that the author called this a "starter" recipe (she recommends modifying it to your own pleasure, yes?) I made the following changes: 
(a) Instead of the potatoes, I used 1/2 cup corn and 1/2 cup diced green bell pepper. 
(b) Like Kitchenwitch, I sauteed everything in the oil before adding the water.
(c) I served the lentils over big steamy baked potatoes with a dollop of sour cream & chopped cilantro garnish. 
What a *wonderful* dish -- thank you!

This would make a great side dish. I wanted to turn it into a meal so I seasoned some chicken legs with garlic powder, chili powder, salt and pepper and browned them in the pan first, cooked my onions and tomatoes for a few minutes, and then added the remaining ingredients. I did have to add a little extra water, but this made for a wholesome thick chicken stew that I served over rice. It was perfect for a cold night.

This was delicious served over rice with a little cheese and avocado. I did change it up a little though: I doubled the recipe used 2 1/2 cups of lentils, vegetable broth instead of water, canned diced tomatoes, only two teaspoons of cumin, a bunch of minced garlic, some cilantro, a teaspoon of paprika and coriander, a can of corn and used red potatoes. YUMMY!

Very tasty. With some changes, this is a 5 star recipe. It definitely needs more liquid and time to cook, if you don't want hard lentils and potatoes. I used 1 cup vegetable broth and 1 1/2 cups water, and added carrots, garlic, thyme and cayenne pepper. Next time, I might try this in the slow cooker!

Love this recipe!! Made it a little spicy with some habanero pepper and red pepper flakes! Didn’t have potatoes so I used more veggies (corn, peas, carrots etc) added chopped celery and topped it off with some crispy bacon and fresh basil Definitely making this again in my slow cooker!

This is really a great base for anything. When I make it I follow the recipe and then just add anything from my veggie drawer that is needing to be used before going bad. Perfect for the end of the week right before grocery shopping.

This is very good. I followed the recipe exactly, except for adding some minced garlic on the advice of another reviewer. I did have to add 1/2 cup more water when I added the potatoes, just like the other reviewers. I served it as a side dish, but I can see how it could make a great soup or be lovely served over rice as a meatless meal. I will definitely make this again, thanks for the great recipe!

I made this last night and it was GREAT! Everyone loved it as a main dish served over rice. I added a few frozen green peas at the end and I also sauteed the lentils and potatoes with the onion and some garlic before adding the water. I also used curry powder for the seasoning, along with black pepper and sea salt. EXCELLENT!
Tasted great! Just for my own palate seemed like a bit too much cumin.
I made this with 2 cups of water and 3 tsp. of cumin. WOW! Fantastic! This has become a cold weather favorite!
I add finally chopped carrots as well, use chicken broth instead of water. If fresh tomatoes unavailable I get a can of Rotel diced tomatoes or mild store brand.

I added another half a cup of water. I used cherry tomatoes that were very small in this recipe. I used one and a half teaspoons of cumin. I combined the lentils and the potatoes while I was cooking for 45 minutes. Yum yum I love this recipe I'm definitely making it again. 😋
I love the flavor but the second time and on, I added more tomatoes and potatoes
Ok

I am Colombian and I wanted to give my husband and 2 boys a taste of my culture but I couldn’t find my recipe so I went here to see if I could find this recipe and I did and I LOVE IT!!! All thought my husband didn’t want to admit it but he loved it to!!!
I’m glad I followed this recipe. I added chicken stock & garlic powder to it for extra flavor.
was craving something late at night, didn't have too much energy to cook, this was perfect. easy, tasty, healthy, satiating.
